title: Futoshiki with a unique solution
description: Generate a Futoshiki puzzle: an n x n Latin square (every row and column holds 1..n once) with some values shown and some inequality signs between neighbouring cells. The abstraction guesses a solved grid, the cells to show (givens) and the neighbouring pairs that get a sign (signs); the sign points the way the grid does. The check looks for two different grids that fit all shown values and signs; the refinement asks for a value or a sign that fails in one of them. The run stops at the first puzzle.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: The size of the grid, the neighbouring cells and the printed clues. Added to every solver.
fragments.text:
% Futoshiki on an n x n grid: every row and every column holds 1..n once, and an
% inequality sign between two neighbouring cells must hold. An instance may print values
% pre(R,C,V) and signs prelt(R1,C1,R2,C2) (the cell R1,C1 is smaller).
#const n = 5.
row(1..n). col(1..n). val(1..n).
% Neighbouring cells, in both orders.
adj(R,C,R,C+1) :- row(R), col(C), C < n.
adj(R,C,R+1,C) :- row(R), col(C), R < n.
adj(R2,C2,R1,C1) :- adj(R1,C1,R2,C2), (R1,C1) < (R2,C2).
printed(R,C) :- pre(R,C,_).
signed(R1,C1,R2,C2) :- prelt(R1,C1,R2,C2).
signed(R2,C2,R1,C1) :- prelt(R1,C1,R2,C2).

fragments.name: rules
fragments.description: The rules of the puzzle for any grid; used by solver A (one grid) and solver C (two grids).
fragments.text:
% The rules for every grid G that a solver declares with grid(G).
1 { cell(G,R,C,V) : val(V) } 1 :- grid(G), row(R), col(C).
:- cell(G,R,C1,V), cell(G,R,C2,V), C1 < C2.
:- cell(G,R1,C,V), cell(G,R2,C,V), R1 < R2.
% Every grid respects the printed values and signs.
:- grid(G), pre(R,C,V), not cell(G,R,C,V).
:- prelt(R1,C1,R2,C2), cell(G,R1,C1,V1), cell(G,R2,C2,V2), V1 > V2.

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): a solved grid, the cells shown and the pairs that get a sign.
fragments.text:
% A candidate: a solved grid s, the cells whose values are shown, and the neighbouring
% pairs that get a sign.
grid(s).
givens { clue(R,C) : row(R), col(C), not printed(R,C) } givens.
signs { sign(R1,C1,R2,C2) : adj(R1,C1,R2,C2), (R1,C1) < (R2,C2), not signed(R1,C1,R2,C2) } signs.
% given(R,C,V): the puzzle shows V in row R, column C.
given(R,C,V) :- clue(R,C), cell(s,R,C,V).
% less(R1,C1,R2,C2): the puzzle shows that cell R1,C1 is smaller than cell R2,C2.
less(R1,C1,R2,C2) :- sign(R1,C1,R2,C2), cell(s,R1,C1,V1), cell(s,R2,C2,V2), V1 < V2.
less(R2,C2,R1,C1) :- sign(R1,C1,R2,C2), cell(s,R1,C1,V1), cell(s,R2,C2,V2), V1 > V2.
#show given/3.
#show less/4.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atoms: the shown values and the signs. The solved grid stays private to solver A.
fragments.text:
glue(given(R,C,V)) :- row(R), col(C), val(V), not printed(R,C).
glue(less(R1,C1,R2,C2)) :- adj(R1,C1,R2,C2), not signed(R1,C1,R2,C2).

fragments.name: check
fragments.description: Looks for two different grids that fit the shown values and signs (solver C).
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: two different grids a and b that both fit the shown values and signs.
grid(a). grid(b).
:- given(R,C,V), not cell(a,R,C,V).
:- given(R,C,V), not cell(b,R,C,V).
:- less(R1,C1,R2,C2), cell(G,R1,C1,V1), cell(G,R2,C2,V2), V1 > V2.
differ :- cell(a,R,C,V), not cell(b,R,C,V).
:- not differ.
#show.
#show a(R,C,V) : cell(a,R,C,V).
#show b(R,C,V) : cell(b,R,C,V).

% Both grids fit every puzzle that shows only values and signs that hold in both. So the
% puzzle must show a value or a sign that fails in a or in b.
both(R,C,V) :- cell(a,R,C,V), cell(b,R,C,V).
relevant(given(R,C,V)) :- row(R), col(C), val(V), not printed(R,C), not both(R,C,V).
smaller(G,R1,C1,R2,C2) :- adj(R1,C1,R2,C2), cell(G,R1,C1,V1), cell(G,R2,C2,V2), V1 < V2.
relevant(less(R1,C1,R2,C2)) :- adj(R1,C1,R2,C2), not signed(R1,C1,R2,C2),
    not smaller(a,R1,C1,R2,C2).
relevant(less(R1,C1,R2,C2)) :- adj(R1,C1,R2,C2), not signed(R1,C1,R2,C2),
    not smaller(b,R1,C1,R2,C2).

fragments.name: view
fragments.description: A domain view (Observatory tab): the scene part draws what stays, the frame part one step, as draw/1 marks.
fragments.text:
% Cells at odd rows and columns; between two neighbours a slot for the sign.
#program scene.
draw(layout(grid)).
draw(cell(2*R-1,2*C-1)) :- row(R), col(C).
slot(R,C,2*R-1,2*C) :- row(R), col(C), C < n.
slot(R,C,2*R,2*C-1) :- row(R), col(C), R < n.
draw(cell(X,Y)) :- slot(_,_,X,Y).
draw(attr(cell(2*R-1,2*C-1), label, V)) :- pre(R,C,V).
draw(attr(cell(2*R-1,2*C-1), fill, printed)) :- pre(R,C,_).
% A sign: < or > between columns, ^ or v between rows (pointing at the smaller cell).
sign(X,Y,"<") :- slot(R,C,X,Y), X \ 2 == 1, prelt(R,C,R,C+1).
sign(X,Y,">") :- slot(R,C,X,Y), X \ 2 == 1, prelt(R,C+1,R,C).
sign(X,Y,"^") :- slot(R,C,X,Y), X \ 2 == 0, prelt(R,C,R+1,C).
sign(X,Y,"v") :- slot(R,C,X,Y), X \ 2 == 0, prelt(R+1,C,R,C).

#program frame.
sign(X,Y,"<") :- slot(R,C,X,Y), X \ 2 == 1, cand(less(R,C,R,C+1)).
sign(X,Y,">") :- slot(R,C,X,Y), X \ 2 == 1, cand(less(R,C+1,R,C)).
sign(X,Y,"^") :- slot(R,C,X,Y), X \ 2 == 0, cand(less(R,C,R+1,C)).
sign(X,Y,"v") :- slot(R,C,X,Y), X \ 2 == 0, cand(less(R+1,C,R,C)).
draw(attr(cell(X,Y), label, S)) :- sign(X,Y,S).
draw(attr(cell(X,Y), fill, sign)) :- sign(X,Y,_).
draw(ghost(cell(X,Y))) :- slot(_,_,X,Y), not sign(X,Y,_).
draw(attr(cell(2*R-1,2*C-1), label, V)) :- cand(given(R,C,V)).
draw(attr(cell(2*R-1,2*C-1), fill, clue)) :- cand(given(R,C,_)).
differs(R,C,(V,W)) :- cex(a(R,C,V)), cex(b(R,C,W)), V != W.
draw(attr(cell(2*R-1,2*C-1), fill, differ)) :- differs(R,C,_).
draw(attr(cell(2*R-1,2*C-1), label, L)) :- differs(R,C,L).
draw(note("Two solutions fit the values and signs; they differ in the coloured cells (a, b).")) :- kind(reject).
draw(note("One solution: the puzzle is done.")) :- kind(solution).
#show draw/1.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + rules + abstraction
solver C = shared + rules + check      options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

instances.facts:
% No printed clues: a 5 x 5 puzzle with no values and 7 signs (6 do not finish in
% two minutes).
% All 3 x 3 puzzles with three signs and one solution (checked by brute force).
% 3 x 3 with one value and two signs: 2,944 puzzles.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + rules + abstraction
solver C = shared + rules + check      options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# The blocking loop: every refuted candidate is blocked on its own.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.block(M)

solver A = shared + rules + abstraction
solver C = shared + rules + check      options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Up to 3 counterexamples per candidate, one clause each.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        for X in C.models(assume G(M), limit 3):
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

solver A = shared + rules + abstraction   options "--enum-mode=record"
solver C = shared + rules + check      options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

generators.name: printed
generators.description: A random n x n Latin square (the cyclic square with its rows, columns and values permuted); each cell printed with probability p/1000 and each neighbouring pair gets its sign with probability q/1000. Set the instance constant n to the same value.
generators.text:
% printed: the cyclic Latin square with rows, columns and values permuted at random; values printed with probability p/1000, signs with q/1000
row(1..n). col(1..n).
g(@perm(n, R, rows),@perm(n, C, cols),@perm(n, (R+C-2)\n+1, vals)) :- row(R), col(C).
pre(R,C,V) :- g(R,C,V), @flip(p, R, C, show) = 1.
pair(R,C,R,C+1) :- row(R), col(C), C < n.
pair(R,C,R+1,C) :- row(R), col(C), R < n.
prelt(R1,C1,R2,C2) :- pair(R1,C1,R2,C2), g(R1,C1,V1), g(R2,C2,V2), V1 < V2, @flip(q, R1, C1, R2, C2) = 1.
prelt(R2,C2,R1,C1) :- pair(R1,C1,R2,C2), g(R1,C1,V1), g(R2,C2,V2), V1 > V2, @flip(q, R1, C1, R2, C2) = 1.
#show pre/3.  #show prelt/4.
